findings.text: The W-1 skeleton only asks that a search finds by title or author. It should also reject the plausible wrong implementations. (1) Matching over the whole record or JSON: q=Priya must give M5, otherwise the search reveals who reserved a book (T-18), and `claim` tokens must not match either. (2) Searching condition, a non-goal: b1's seeded condition holds 'Bookplates', and q=bookplates must give M5. 'Coffee ring' is another check. (3) Concatenating fields: q='darkness ursula' must not match across title and author. (4) Building a RegExp from the term: q='(' must give M5 with status 200, not a 500, and q='.' must match only literal dots, for example 'J. L. Carr' and 'Ursula K. Le Guin', not the whole shelf. Also prove trimming and case with '  LE GUIN  ' finding exactly two books, via the form's `+` encoding. Prove q= and q=%20%20 show the whole shelf with no '0 books match' line. Prove b2 appears in a search marked reserved with no Reserve link, and that a free result keeps its link.

findings.text: I-3 (T-18) and I-5 (T-16) are obligations of this unit, but their witnesses go through `flowPages()` and fixed paths, none of which is a search page. Without a change, both stay green without ever seeing a results page or an M5 page. Add a matching search and a no-match search to the pages those witnesses walk. Only add to them; keep the existing assertions.

Build the match to tolerate non-string fields. `loadShelf` does not validate book fields, and the corpus says the keeper hand-edits this file. Today `/` renders a numeric title and a missing author without failing, because esc calls String(). A naive `book.title.toLowerCase()` would make every search return a 500 while `/` stays fine. Use String(book.title ?? '') or similar, and cover it with a test.

findings.text: Design details the spec leaves implicit but D1 pulls in. The form is `<form role="search" method="get" action="/">`, with visible label 'Find a book by title or author', one text input named q and a button 'Search'. M5 counts as a refusal under the M2 to M8 rules: its title is `No match for "{q}"`, its heading and body come first in `<main>` in the refusal block, then the form with q still in the box, then the 'Show the whole shelf' link, and no books are listed. The explicit M5 order wins over the general line in the announcing section saying the back link follows directly. Tie the search input to the refusal with aria-describedby, as the markup rules ask. Do not add autofocus: that rule covers M4, M6 and M7 only. Results show the line `2 books match "le guin"` above the list plus the link. The design gives only the plural, so use '1 book matches' for one result. Results need their own `<title>`, because every page must have a distinct one and the design names none for results. Show the trimmed term, and leave the box empty for a blank search.

Existing field and button styles are scoped to `.slip`, and `.slip button` is rust-filled. The design makes the search button outlined (rust text on paper, 2px rust border) and keeps the Reserve form's button as the only filled shape. So reusing `class="slip"` as it stands draws the search button wrongly. Share the field rule and add the outlined variant, keeping 44px targets, a 2px ink input border and max-width 100%. No sideways scrolling at 360px needs checking in the walkthrough with a long unbroken q. `body { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` already covers the echoed text.

Scope guards. (1) Put the form in the shelf and no-match pages, not in `layout()`: existing tests require the confirmation and just-taken pages to have no form. (2) Every page function defaults `settings = DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, so a new no-match page or a missed argument silently shows the default name, breaking I-20 for a custom shelf. Pass settings through and prove it with createApp({ settings }). (3) I-21 is listed in the obligations, but it is `activation: future` and delivered by settings-file, and the window line is not rendered today. This unit does not need to build it. Keep the form positioned so the line can later go above `<main>` as the design describes.

premises.claim: F1 holds: the seed has exactly two books by Ursula K. Le Guin, and no other title or author contains 'le guin'.

Search needs no new route: GET / already parses the URL with URL, and searchParams tolerates malformed escapes without throwing (checked with `new URL` for %ZZ, %E0%A4%A and le+guin), so a bad q cannot reach the 500 path through parsing.
Reusing bookItem keeps Reserve links and reserved marks, and applies isHeld so a lapsed hold shows as free in results.
